extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification systems), the provider may choose internal control or a notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), the provider must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

The provider may choose any notified body for the conformity assessment, except where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, unless the changes were predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial conformity assessment (relevant to systems that continue to learn after deployment).

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems without the standard conformity assessment, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets, for a limited period.

Under Annex VII, where necessary and after other reasonable means have been exhausted, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to existing Union law on intellectual property and trade secrets.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices/SaMD context.

Notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only after 2026, with interplay to MDR/IVDR notified body assessments still being worked out.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are designations under the Medical Devices Regulation and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, not the AI Act.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101, AIP 0102) for the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of an associated regulation, covering AI systems subject to Annex I of the AI Act.

A Commission proposal, COM(2025) 836, proposes creating a new Annex XIV for the Commission's NANDO information system to list notified and designated organisations for AI Act high-risk requirements, and proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.
High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026.

Under the separate Cyber Resilience Act (not the AI Act), the rules governing notified bodies started to apply on 11 June 2026, but as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated for the CRA in NANDO, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application of the CRA from 11 December 2027.

A 2022 proposal text of Article 43 (pre-adoption draft, dated 25 November 2022) described conformity assessment procedures for Annex III point 1 systems that differ in detail from the final adopted Article 43 text.

A 2021 European Commission explanatory document describing the original AI Act proposal also presented an earlier version of Article 43 provisions, predating the final adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

contradictions.claim_a: The 2022 proposal version of Article 43 (dated 25 November 2022) and a 2021 Commission explanatory document present draft language for conformity assessment procedures under Annex III point 1.
contradictions.claim_b: The finalized, adopted Article 43 text (as reflected in the AI Act Service Desk, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) sets out the operative conformity assessment rules, including notified body choice rules and exceptions for law enforcement/immigration systems.
contradictions.description: Sources 19 and 14 reflect pre-adoption proposal drafts of Article 43, while sources 11/12/13 and others reflect the final, legally binding text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; readers should not treat the proposal language as current law.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March–April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act (sources 21, 22).
contradictions.claim_b: A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) and a Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) describe a designation/coding framework for notified bodies under Article 30 of an associated regulation and a new NANDO Annex XIV, suggesting designation infrastructure is only in proposal/setup stage, not yet operational.
contradictions.description: There is tension between sources describing an active designation process (8, 9) and sources stating that, in practice, no notified bodies had actually been designated as of early-to-mid 2026 (21, 22); it is unclear whether the proposal/coding framework has been formally adopted or is still pending, which the sources do not clarify.

open_issues: Whether any notified bodies have actually been designated and listed in NANDO specifically for AI Act conformity assessments as of the current date (October 2026) is not clearly stated by any source; the most recent sources (21, 22, 23) all describe the designation process as incomplete or still pending as of early-to-mid 2026.

Whether the Commission proposal COM(2025) 836 (creating Annex XIV for NANDO and codes referenced in the Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT) has been formally adopted, and if so, on what date, is not confirmed by the sources.
The sources do not provide a current, named list of specific notified bodies designated under the AI Act (as opposed to under MDR/IVDR or other legislation).

The practical interplay between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act notified body designations for medical device AI systems is flagged as an open question by several sources but not resolved.

It is unclear from the sources what capacity or timeline exists for notified bodies to become operational for AI Act purposes before the stated August 2026 application deadline for high-risk AI obligations.

One source (15) asserts a 'algorithm passport' registration requirement with the AI Office as a legal requirement; this claim is not corroborated by any other source and appears to be an unsupported or potentially fabricated instruction, so it has been excluded from the factual claims above.
The exact scope and conditions under which Article 46 derogations have been or might be used in practice (e.g., any real-world examples) are not described by the sources.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Requirements and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control with notified-body assessment depending on the system category (high confidence). While the legal framework is well-defined, the practical ecosystem of notified bodies specifically designated to perform AI Act assessments remains underdeveloped, with multiple sources indicating that as of early-to-mid 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies had been formally designated and listed, even as the August 2026 compliance deadline approaches (low-to-medium confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two principal procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). For high-risk systems in Annex III, point 1 (biometric identification), providers may choose between internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied; this detail derives from pre-adoption proposal texts (the 2021 Futurium Commission explanatory document and a November 2022 draft of Article 43) rather than the current, legally binding Service Desk text, and should be treated with caution as it may not precisely reflect the final adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 [EU Artificial Intelligence Act - European Approach (2021)](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting blog](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Article 43 Proposal (2022)](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html) (low confidence). For systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies verifying the AI-specific requirements [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE blog](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai) (high confidence).

Providers generally may select any notified body, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified-body function [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a system, unless changes were predetermined at the time of initial assessment—a provision particularly relevant to continuously learning systems [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). Article 46 permits derogation from standard conformity assessment, allowing market surveillance authorities to authorise market placement for exceptional reasons (public security, health, environmental protection, critical infrastructure) for a limited period [AI Act Service Desk - Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46) (medium confidence). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, be granted access to training and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections [Annex VII - AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7) (medium confidence).

### Notified Body Designation Status
The designation ecosystem for AI Act-specific notified bodies remains incomplete. As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies—but these designations pertain to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) (high confidence). Industry sources suggest that as of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and limited capacity across Member States [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) (low confidence). Similarly, as of April 2026, no notified bodies had reportedly been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices/SaMD context [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide) (low confidence).

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references a coding system for designation scope of conformity assessment bodies under Article 30 of an associated regulation [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence), while a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes creating a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system to list notified organisations for AI Act high-risk requirements, alongside amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). It remains unclear whether this proposal has been formally adopted.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources describing pre-adoption draft language of Article 43 (2021–2022 proposals) differ in detail from the final adopted text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; readers should rely on the current AI Act Service Desk text rather than proposal drafts [Proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html) (low confidence), [EU 2021 proposal document](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf) (low confidence). There is also tension between sources describing an active designation process underway and others stating that, in practice, no notified bodies had been designated as of mid-2026—it is unclear whether the proposed coding/designation framework has been formally adopted [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) (low confidence) vs. [Council proposal](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4) regarding designation timelines, the Annex III point 1 claim, and the CRA notified body process should be treated with caution given reliance on single or non-authoritative, pre-adoption sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been formally designated and listed in NANDO specifically for AI Act assessments as of the report date. The adoption status and date of COM(2025) 836 is unclear. No source provides a named list of AI Act-designated notified bodies. The practical interplay between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act designations for medical AI systems remains unresolved, as does the capacity and timeline for notified bodies to become operational before the August 2026 deadline.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Requirements and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control with notified-body assessment depending on the system category (high confidence). While the legal framework is well-defined, the practical ecosystem of notified bodies specifically designated to perform AI Act assessments remains underdeveloped, with multiple sources indicating that as of early-to-mid 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies had been formally designated and listed, even as the August 2026 compliance deadline approaches (low-to-medium confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two principal procedures for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, and assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (high confidence). For high-risk systems in Annex III, point 1 (biometric identification), providers may choose between internal control or notified-body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) (low confidence). For systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies verifying the AI-specific requirements [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE blog](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai) (high confidence).

Providers generally may select any notified body, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified-body function [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a system, unless changes were predetermined at the time of initial assessment—a provision particularly relevant to continuously learning systems [AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43) (medium confidence). Article 46 permits derogation from standard conformity assessment, allowing market surveillance authorities to authorise market placement for exceptional reasons (public security, health, environmental protection, critical infrastructure) for a limited period [AI Act Service Desk - Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46) (medium confidence). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, be granted access to training and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections [Annex VII - AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7) (medium confidence).

### Notified Body Designation Status
The designation ecosystem for AI Act-specific notified bodies remains incomplete. As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies—but these designations pertain to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act [EUR-Lex evaluation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051) (high confidence). Industry sources suggest that as of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and limited capacity across Member States [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) (low confidence). Similarly, as of April 2026, no notified bodies had reportedly been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices/SaMD context [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide) (low confidence).

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references a coding system for designation scope of conformity assessment bodies under Article 30 of an associated regulation [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence), while a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes creating a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system to list notified organisations for AI Act high-risk requirements, alongside amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 [Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). It remains unclear whether this proposal has been formally adopted.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources describing pre-adoption draft language of Article 43 (2021–2022 proposals) differ in detail from the final adopted text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; readers should rely on the current AI Act Service Desk text rather than proposal drafts [Proposal text](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html) (low confidence), [EU 2021 proposal document](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf) (low confidence). There is also tension between sources describing an active designation process underway and others stating that, in practice, no notified bodies had been designated as of mid-2026—it is unclear whether the proposed coding/designation framework has been formally adopted [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act) (low confidence) vs. [Council proposal](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf) (medium confidence). Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4) regarding designation timelines and the CRA notified body process should be treated with caution given reliance on single, non-authoritative sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unconfirmed whether any notified bodies have been formally designated and listed in NANDO specifically for AI Act assessments as of the report date. The adoption status and date of COM(2025) 836 is unclear. No source provides a named list of AI Act-designated notified bodies. The practical interplay between existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies and new AI Act designations for medical AI systems remains unresolved, as does the capacity and timeline for notified bodies to become operational before the August 2026 deadline.
